<p class="eyebrow">Plotting</p>

# Semantic plots

::: {.doc-lead}
A plot with named parts remains editable after it leaves Python.
:::

Most tools treat a saved plot as a picture. Flux treats it as a **structure**: when a plot is
made with [fluxplot](https://github.com/fluxsci/fluxplot), every meaningful part of it — a
series' line, its 4th data point, the x-axis title — carries a **stable name**. That one idea is
what makes Flux figures feel alive:

- **Click into a plot and restyle a part** — one line's colour, one label's size — in the
  [Figure workspace](/docs/figure.html), without touching your analysis code.
- **Regenerate without losing your tuning.** Re-run the analysis script and the plot updates in
  place; your per-part restyles survive, because they're keyed to the part *names*, not to
  pixels.
- **Animate at the level of parts** in the [Slides workspace](/docs/slides.html) — fade one
  series in, draw a curve on, morph one chart into another.

## Every part has a name {#every-part-has-a-name}

Hover the plot below. The box of one condition, the median line inside it, a single point, the
tick labels of the x axis: each is its own element in the saved SVG, and each carries an id that
Flux, your captions, your animations and your agent all use to refer to it.

## What fluxplot is {#what-fluxplot-is}

`fluxplot` is an ordinary Python library you use in your analysis environment — "matplotlib,
but every meaningful thing has a name." You plot through thin helpers that take a series name,
then save with `fp.save()`:

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import fluxplot as fp

fp.use_light()   # the house style: Flexoki palette, clean axes

# t, control and treatment come from your analysis of data/growth.csv.
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.4, 4.8))
fp.line(ax, t, control,   series="control",   marker="o", label="Control")
fp.line(ax, t, treatment, series="treatment", marker="s", label="Treatment")
ax.set_xlabel("Time (h)")
ax.set_ylabel("OD600")
fp.legend(ax)

fp.save(fig, "plots/growth.svg", recipe={"inputs": ["data/growth.csv"]})
```

Saving into your project's `plots/` folder writes **three files that travel together**:

```
plots/growth.svg            ← the plot, with named, addressable parts
plots/growth.fluxplot.json  ← the manifest: data, coordinates, parts inventory
plots/growth.recipe.json    ← the recipe: how it was made, so it can be re-made
```

Name series consistently across related plots: the name is the handle Flux restyles by.
When saving from a Python script, fluxplot discovers the script automatically, so the recipe
above only adds the input file. Pass `"params"` as well when the script takes parameters (see
[Recipes and parameters](/docs/save-and-recipes.html#recipes-and-parameters)), or
`recipe=False` to suppress script discovery. Installation and a complete first script are in
the [fluxplot quickstart](/docs/fluxplot.html); every function is listed in the
[Python API reference](/docs/fluxplot-api.html).

## True physical size {#true-physical-size}

Plots import at their **true printed size**: a matplotlib `figsize=(6.4, 4.8)` panel lands on
the canvas at exactly 6.4 × 4.8 inches, and what you lay out is what prints. Flux never silently
rescales an import to fit — if a plot is bigger than its figure frame, it overflows visibly
(with a toast pointing at **Ctrl+Shift+I** to bring it inside). Sizing decisions belong to you
and your plotting code, not to an importer.

## Regenerate, don't re-save {#regenerate-dont-re-save}

To change a plot, **re-run the script** rather than hand-editing the output. With the app open,
the regenerated plot hot-swaps into your figures live, restyles intact. And because the recipe
records the script, its parameters, and its inputs, a plot can be regenerated *with different
parameters* — from the app or the command line — without editing code.

## What about plots from anywhere else? {#what-about-plots-from-anywhere-else}

Other SVGs also import with an automatically derived parts tree for editing and animation;
PNGs remain images. Derived SVG parts do not carry the original scientific data or a recipe;
fluxplot supplies that additional meaning. If a plot saved by fluxplot imports as a flat
image, something is wrong, and `flux validate-plot plots/<name>.svg` says what.

## Multiple panels and precise data {#multiple-panels-and-precise-data}

From schema 0.3, fluxplot keeps each subplot's series and axes separate, including shared
axes, twins and insets. Give panels stable names before plotting when their layout may change:

```python
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, layout="constrained")
fp.panel(axes[0], "baseline")
fp.panel(axes[1], "followup")
```

Both panels can now use `series="control"` without merging their identities. Ordinary single-panel
plots retain their existing part names. Saving after editing captures the current artist data;
small scientific values keep their precision, and missing observations remain gaps.

Slides use each series' owning axes when interpolating data. A matching line/scatter plot with
supported linear or logarithmic axes can morph in data space. Polar/3D projections, unsupported
scales, field layers and other composite plots use the complete transition behavior. Existing
projects stay readable; upgrading does not regenerate your plots automatically.

## Matrices, contours and colour scales {#matrices-contours-and-color-scales}

Use `fp.heatmap`, `fp.contour`, `fp.contourf` and `fp.colorbar` to name the field and its key:

```python
# matrix comes from your analysis.
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
image = fp.heatmap(ax, matrix, series="correlation", cmap="viridis", vmin=0, vmax=1)
fp.colorbar(image, name="correlation", label="Correlation")
fp.save(fig, "plots/correlation.svg")
```

For a modest matrix, `cells=True` makes individual cells addressable. Large fields stay efficient
as one named raster layer. Raw matrix values are only included when `include_values=True`. The
[matrices and colour scales guide](/docs/matrices-and-scales.html) covers fields in detail.

### Recolour a plot without Python {#recolour-without-python}

A plot saved with fluxplot schema 0.3.1 or later records each colour scale's exact law (the
colormap table, the normalization and its limits) and the data value of every coloured
element, so Flux can recolour the plot itself:

- Select the plot and edit **Colour scales** in the Object inspector, or **colour scale** in its
  **F** menu. The palette, its direction, the norm kind, the limits and `extend` change live,
  together with the colorbar. The edit is saved with the figure or slide, and tweens in a talk.
- **Apply to source** writes the complete colour controls into the recipe (`__fluxplot__`,
  keyed by the series name) and regenerates the plot from the source data, keeping your
  named-part overrides. It needs a runnable recipe and affects only that plot's save, leaving
  sibling outputs untouched.

Plots saved with an older schema offer only the palette and range fields in the **X-ray**, and
those regenerate the plot.

### Series colours and deck themes {#series-colours-and-themes}

The manifest also records each series' **colour** (its hex value and, when fluxplot drew it from
a palette, the exact palette token) and the **theme token** of every scaffold element. With it,
Flux can give a whole series one colour (**Series colour** in the Plot part section, or
`set-series-color` from the command line), and a plot on a slide can
[follow the deck theme](/docs/transforms.html#plots-follow-the-deck-theme): its ink, axes and
gridlines take the theme's colours, while data colours never change.

### Read the data back {#read-the-data-back}

`flux get-plot-data` returns what the plot shows: every series' exact values and per-point IDs,
hexmatrix bins, glowbar and fluxbox statistics, heatmap values, image channels, axis domains,
and each significance bracket's test and p-value. Long arrays are windowed. In Flux, hold
**Ctrl** while hovering a part to see the same facts on the canvas.

### What schema 0.3.2 adds {#what-schema-032-adds}

- A colour scale can carry an **opacity channel** (`alpha_by`, for example a hexagon's count
  or a cell's p-value), which recolours live with the palette.
- **Twin value axes** (`ax.twinx()` and secondary axes) get their own axis view.
- Bars, cells and hexagons carry **stable keys** and their data boxes, so an axis view moves
  them and a Become between two versions of a plot tweens them member by member.
- Every axis records its **tick scheme**, so a viewed axis is re-ticked.
- Fits (`fp.regression`, `fp.kde`), steps, stems, images and the figure's own title, legend and
  annotations are named parts that `get-plot-data` and the hover readout report.

Two kinds of ID changed in 0.3.2: spines are now named like `axis.x.spine.bottom`, and some
series names are spelled differently so they no longer collide. The manifest's `idAliases` maps
the old IDs, so overrides, captions and effects saved against an older plot keep pointing at the
same parts.

### Checks on import {#checks-on-import}

New imports and linked-source reloads verify the SVG/manifest checksum before accepting the
bundle. If generation is still writing files or the sidecar belongs to another SVG, Flux keeps
the last accepted plot and reports the mismatch. This check runs before any repair of older
SVGs.
